Assistant Directors / Ralph W. Larson Ronald N. Andrews
Arthur S. Coffin, Yakima, Chairman Harold A. Pehhles, Olympia Elmer G. Gerken, Quincy James R. Agen, LaConner Glenn Galbraith, Wellpinis Claude Bekins, Seattle
Game Cenimission
DEPARTMENT OF GAME
600 North Capitol Way / Olympia, Washington 98504
April 25, 1972
Mr. Yates M. Barber, Acting Chief Office of Environmental Quality Bureau of Sport Fisheries & Wildlife Washington, D. C. 20240
Dear Mr. Barber:
We have reviewed the draft environmental statement you refer to as proposed Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972.
This proposal outlined is an indication of long-needed legislation in the important fields of wildlife management and ecology. It certainly reflects the changing attitudes of citizens toward wildlife and the environment. For this we commend your action.
There are a few general comments we feel should be made before discussing details of the statement.
1. State jurisdiction over resident wildlife must be maintained at its traditional level. These responsibilities can not be aborgated by the states nor assumed by the federal government if the existing balance is to be maintained. Your statement does not clearly spell out this important point; we suggest your final statement do so.
2. The general thesis of the draft emphasizes protection aspects as major means of accomplishing the goal of improving the status of endangered species. We feel that greater stress should be placed upon acquisition and/or preservation of habitats upon which these species are dependent if they are to survive.
3. Certain animals included in current endangered species categories are indeed in a tenuous position on portions of their ranges. However, there are other portions of the range where habitat conditions and management programs are such that they enjoy a more-favorable status. On these areas, prohibitions against consumntive use might actually operate at cross purposes to your goal. You do treat the situation briefly, but we feel that this point needs strengthening. We suggest that it appear in the "Description of the Proposal" section of your statement, as well as in other sections where you discuss the dynamics of ecosystems and uses of the resource.
